โรงเจในสวน หรือศาลเจ้าเซ้งเหล่งเก้ง ปราก: Rong Jae Nai Suan, or Seng Leng Keng Shrine, appears in Takua Pa Town Municipality documents as a centuries-old shrine, but the same documents do not give its construction year. It is therefore not yet possible to place its beginnings in a particular reign.
ผู้ก่อตั้งที่เอกสารเทศบาลระบุคือ นายส้อ: The founder identified in municipal documents is Mr So Thian Seng, an overseas Chinese settler. After the shrine was completed, Phra Cheng Chui Cho Sue, or Chao Pho Yat Nam Khang, was brought from China and enshrined there. The place therefore likely served both as a site of worship and as a centre of belief for the Chinese community in the mining and port town of Takua Pa. However, there is no site-specific evidence for its construction year, the founder's policy rationale, or its everyday role at the time.
เอกสารท้องถิ่นอีกชุดเล่าว่านายส้อเส็งเคย: Another local document says that Mr So Seng had worked with Ku Chai Tung Shrine before opening the shrine in the garden. However, it cannot yet be confirmed that he was the same person as Mr So Thian Seng, so these are not presented as the same fact.
ไม่พบปีหรือเหตุการณ์ที่ยืนยันได้: No confirmed year or event has been found
จากแหล่งที่ตรวจสอบได้ ยังไม่พบหลักฐานว่า: Among the verifiable sources, no evidence has been found that the shrine changed ownership, was abandoned, or was restored in any particular year. No site-specific evidence has been found showing how the 2004 tsunami (พ.ศ. 2547) affected this building.
ยังไม่พบรายการขึ้นทะเบียนโบราณสถานของโรง: No historic-site registration entry has been found for Rong Jae Nai Suan, and there is no information that it was converted to another business or type of public building. The verifiable information for the intervening period is therefore limited to the continuity of the place name and memories of an old shrine. The history of another shrine in the old town should not be used to fill the gaps.
บริบทเมืองตะกั่วป่าเปลี่ยนจากเมืองเหมือง: Takua Pa's context changed from a mining and maritime-trading town into a historic and cultural town, but the sources found do not yet connect this city-level change with specific events at Rong Jae Nai Suan.
ปัจจุบันแหล่งข้อมูลออนไลน์ที่ตรวจสอบได้ย: Currently, verifiable online sources do not confirm who manages the shrine, whether it is open to visitors every day, what condition the building is in, or whether any restoration project is under way. It should therefore not be described as an open tourist attraction or as a place that can be visited without an appointment.
หลักฐานร่วมสมัยที่พบคือบทความรีวิวซึ่งรา: The contemporary evidence found is a review article reporting the sale of ko sui sweets at Rong Jae Nai Suan during the Vegetarian Festival. This indicates that the place was still used for a community festival activity, but it is a blog report, not a shrine schedule announcement, and does not confirm that the activity is held every year.
สำหรับผู้เดินทาง ควรใช้ที่อยู่ระดับซอยโร: Travellers should use the Soi Rong Phra, Thanon Rat Bamrung address as a starting point and check with local people or the municipality before travelling, because no verified coordinates, opening hours, telephone number, or official contact channel are available.
เทศบาลเมืองตะกั่วป่า: เอกสารข้อมูลสถานที: Takua Pa Town Municipality: Place Information Document
เอกสารแผนการดำเนินงานด้านสิ่งแวดล้อมของเ: Takua Pa Town Municipality's environmental action plan documents say that Rong Jae Nai Suan is called Seng Leng Keng Shrine and is more than a century old, without specifying an exact construction year. The municipality identifies its founder as Mr So Thian Seng, an overseas Chinese settler.
องค์เทพที่เทศบาลระบุว่าประดิษฐานในศาลเจ้: The deity that the municipality says is enshrined at the shrine is also known as Chao Pho Yat Nam Khang and is said to have been brought from China. The Hroi Jang blog reports that Ama Tan Si Lun sells ko sui sweets at Rong Jae Nai Suan during the Vegetarian Festival. This is blog information, and sales in the year of travel still need to be checked.

ก่อนมีอาคารถาวร โรงเรียนเต้าหมิงเปิดสอนภ: Before it had a permanent building, Tao Ming School informally taught Chinese through private instruction. When the Private Schools Act of 1918 (พ.ศ. 2461) came into effect, the school formally declared its intention to be established in 1920 (พ.ศ. 2463), using the name “To Beng” in Hokkien pronunciation, before changing to “Tao Ming” in Mandarin pronunciation. The name conveys the idea of leading toward knowledge.
อาคารที่ยังเห็นอยู่สร้างขึ้นใน พ.ศ. 2465: The surviving building was constructed in 1922 (พ.ศ. 2465) with funds collected from mining magnates and Chinese merchants in the old market at Yan Yao, as well as merchant networks from Ranong and Phuket. Another official source describes it as the work of a Chinese merchants' association that entered the tin-mining industry to provide Chinese-language education for Chinese children. The adapted Sino-Portuguese building with its corrugated-metal roof was therefore not only a school, but evidence that wealth from mining, trade, and Chinese networks was becoming a community institution.
ในเวลานั้นตะกั่วป่าเป็นย่านการค้าและขนส่: At that time, Takua Pa was a trading and transport district connected to the river and sea. The town grew through tin, while Chinese people from Hokkien, Guangdong, and Hainan came as workers, merchants, and entrepreneurs. The school helped give the Chinese community in the flourishing mining town a linguistic and cultural foundation.
แหล่งข้อมูลท้องถิ่นระบุว่าเหมืองแร่ตะกั่: Local sources state that Takua Pa's mines gradually closed from the 1970s, reducing the town's activity, while Tao Ming School ceased operations later. Verifiable official sources confirm only that “the school has been discontinued” and that the building is under the care of the Tao Ming School Foundation, Takua Pa. They do not specify the year it ceased operating or details of any change in ownership.
ยังไม่พบหลักฐานอ่านได้ที่ยืนยันว่าอาคารไ: No readable evidence has been found confirming that the building was directly affected by the 2004 tsunami (พ.ศ. 2547) or that it underwent restoration in any particular year. It should therefore not be concluded that it was damaged or repaired because of that event, even though the Takua Pa area has sites connected with tsunami survivor assistance and the old town has regained a cultural-tourism role.
